html:
SMTO-TSK-0039 — The task you chose to wait for can't be used

GUID: 8af7bc33-0db1-4c66-9cf0-4d0e554b07e1
Slug: task-board-dependency-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The task picked in Depends on can't be used. It may be missing, be this same task, belong to another conversation, or create a loop. The new task wasn't added.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page so the Depends on list in the message box shows this conversation's current tasks. The task you picked may have been deleted or changed since the list was loaded.
  2. In Depends on, choose a different task from this same conversation, or choose No dependency — run independently. A task can only wait for another task in its own conversation, never for itself or for a task that waits on it.
  3. Send your message again. The new task wasn't added, so sending it again won't create a duplicate.
  4. If you saw this in the Agent's activity rather than when sending a message, let the Agent continue. The Agent's own step plan follows the same rules and the Agent usually corrects it.

What success looks like

  • Your message appears in the Queued list or starts running, waiting for the task you picked if you chose one.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep sending the same message with different choices; check the Queued list first so you don't create duplicates.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A task dependency was rejected: missing or invalid target, self-reference, duplicate edge, cycle, target in a different conversation, unreadable upstream dependency data, or both an explicit selection and the previous-task option supplied; the model's task board applies the same missing-task and cycle rules.

What this means

  • Task dependencies have missing/invalid targets, duplicate/self/cyclic edges, cross-conversation scope, unreadable upstream structure or competing explicit/previous-task selectors. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Task dependencies have missing/invalid targets, duplicate/self/cyclic edges, cross-conversation scope, unreadable upstream structure or competing explicit/previous-task selectors.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific dependency code and exact target scope, distinguishing structural errors from waiting for unfinished work.

How to fix it

  • Read the dependency code in the message (DEPENDENCY_SELF_REFERENCE, DEPENDENCY_DUPLICATE, DEPENDENCY_CYCLE_DETECTED, DEPENDENCY_INVALID_SCOPE, DEPENDENCY_INVALID_TARGET or DEPENDENCY_INTENT_CONFLICT). Send one dependency for an existing task in the same conversation without the previous-task option and keep the graph acyclic; for manage_tasks, depends_on must name existing board task IDs without cycles. An invalid-target result on an existing chain means an upstream task's stored dependencies_json is unreadable and needs inspection.
  • Correct the specific target, scope or graph violation while preserving the intended ordering.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • All declared links are unique, acyclic and valid within the intended task scope.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
